system_prompt: Select the single RedCrown MCP tool that best satisfies the user's request. Return exactly one tool name and no other text. Do not execute the tool.

tools.name: prove_task
tools.description: Run a fresh benchmark: RedCrown executes models on your task and returns the cheapest one that's good enough, with a shareable proof link. Pass a plain-language task and a few examples ({input, output?}); leave the output blank to rank against the model you use now. If outputs were already generated elsewhere, use import_results. For a no-input demo, use try_sample.

tools.name: try_sample
tools.description: Run a benchmark on a public sample dataset and return a shareable proof — no input, no keys, no account. Great for a quick demo. Optional task (default: transcribe).

tools.name: import_results
tools.description: Import and rank outputs from an eval already run in another harness or the redcrown CLI. This records supplied results and does not execute models. Pass the aggregate results object (name, objective, quality_metric, quality_bar, step, candidates[, references]). Returns the experiment and run ids. To generate fresh outputs, use prove_task.

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: Get an experiment run and its ranked report by run id.

tools.name: get_report
tools.description: Alias of get_run: fetch the ranked proof report for a run id.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: [advanced] List available providers and models, including free no-key models.

tools.name: create_experiment
tools.description: [advanced] Save an experiment from a full definition (name, objective, quality_metric, quality_bar, reference_source, allowed_providers, pipeline, dataset). This does not run it; call run_experiment with the returned experiment id. Most callers should use prove_task instead.

tools.name: run_experiment
tools.description: [advanced] Execute an existing saved experiment by id. This queues model calls and returns the run id to poll with get_report. To draft a definition without creating or running it, use scaffold_experiment.

tools.name: scaffold_experiment
tools.description: [advanced] Draft a valid experiment definition from a plain-language task. This only returns a spec: it does not save an experiment or execute models. Review the spec, then pass it to create_experiment and call run_experiment. (prove_task performs the full flow for you.)

tools.name: simulate_cost
tools.description: [advanced] Estimate projected hosted-API and self-hosted (per cloud) cost for a model and token counts.

tools.name: setup_proxy
tools.description: [advanced] Create a proxied endpoint that captures live traffic for shadow evaluation. Returns the endpoint key and forward URL.

tools.name: list_proxies
tools.description: [advanced] List all proxied endpoints for the caller's workspace.

tools.name: replay_captures
tools.description: [advanced] Replay captured traffic through the shadow eval engine for a proxied endpoint.

tools.name: create_review
tools.description: [advanced] Create a human-review session for a proxied endpoint's captures.

tools.name: invite_reviewer
tools.description: [advanced] Invite a reviewer to a review session. Returns a one-time token; the link is https://app.redcrown.ai/review/<token>.

tools.name: get_review_examples
tools.description: [advanced] Get the candidate outputs for a captured request, ready for human review.

tools.name: get_decision_report
tools.description: [advanced] Get the aggregated decision report for a review session, including reviewer verdicts and the recommended winner.
